J.evidence: Title, description, methods and the cooking object agree with the steps. D-03 classification is plausible for the method and sourcing (not cuisine-driven; sidecar cultural_bias reviewed).

K.evidence: Viewed v5 at full size and in a 2x crop of the cut face. v5 fixes the r2 sheen: the filling is matte, and the curtido and salsa are good. But the bean layer is now a thick (~1/2-inch), uniform, very dark grey-brown slab with a fine, crumbly, granular texture. In the crop it looks like cooked ground beef or a burger patty inside the masa: the 'reads as ground meat' defect self-review rejected v1 and v2 for, and the meat-reading defect from r1 and r2. It also contradicts the recipe in two ways. (1) The ingredient is 'refried small red beans, puréed smooth', which would be a smooth, reddish-brown paste, not crumbly near-black grains. (2) Step 3 mixes the beans and mozzarella into one filling, but the hero shows a separate dark layer with a separate white cheese pull. For a vegetarian meal, a hero filling that reads as ground meat is a fidelity FAIL.
K.fix: Regenerate (v6) and show the filling the recipe makes. Beans and cheese are mixed into one marbled filling: a lighter, reddish-brown, smooth bean paste with melted white mozzarella streaked all through it. It should not be a separate dark layer, and it must have no crumbly or granular texture and no near-black colour. Keep it fairly thin (about 1/4 inch), and keep the masa wall, cheese pull, curtido, salsa and griddle spotting from v5. If the generator still produces a meat-like slab, change the plating so the hero shows two whole spotted pupusas, plus one torn open just enough to show a creamy cheese-and-bean edge. Re-finalize, re-freeze, re-audit K/L.
